correctness.rationale: Each counted jump regenerates the process at G and the waiting times have exponential tails. Let f(z) be their Laplace transform and T=γ+p+s+u+2r. A first-step calculation gives 1/f(z)−1=z(H+Tz+z²)/[γp(q+z)], with q=u+r. Its coefficients through cubic order are A₁=H/(γpq), A₂=(q²−ps)/(γpq²), and A₃=(1/q−T/q²+H/q³)/(γp), using qT−H=q²−ps. For the analytic cumulant-growth exponent λ(k), 1/f(λ(k))−1=e^k−1, so J=1/A₁ and F=1−2A₂J². At equality A₂=0 and A₃=1/(γpq), giving the third normalized cumulant 1−6A₃J³=1−6γ²p²q²/H³. This also verifies the boundary at r=0 and the signs since q is strictly increasing. The waiting-time transform decays as z⁻² at large positive z, incompatible with exponential renewal intervals. The rational example is consistent (H*=24/5); the bundled symbolic checker was inspected, not executed.
